key_insight: DeltaBox achieves millisecond-level checkpoint/rollback by avoiding full-state duplication and instead capturing and restoring only the incremental differences between successive sandbox states (files + process memory/context). This makes frequent state exploration orders of magnitude cheaper.
problem_solved: Current sandbox checkpoint/rollback duplicates entire process and file state, causing hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of latency that block deep search, high-frequency exploration, and large-scale agent fan-out.
method: Exploit high similarity between successive checkpoints to record deltas rather than full copies, dramatically reducing I/O and serialization cost.
Combine copy-on-write/differential snapshotting with lightweight metadata and lazy materialization to enable ultra-fast local checkpoints and rollbacks.
Integrate file- and process-level state capture in the sandbox and perform asynchronous persistence and fast in-memory rebound for rollbacks.
impact: Enables much deeper and wider search (e.g., test-time tree search, RL) and large-scale agent parallelism by reducing C/R latency to the millisecond range, improving throughput and lowering resource cost for stateful AI agents.

paper_title: DeltaBox: Scaling Stateful AI Agents with Millisecond-Level Sandbox Checkpoint/Rollback
paper_authors: Yunpeng Dong, Jingkai He, Yuze Hou, Dong Du, Zhonghu Xu
